ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of each UBO, registered director, legal representative, and signatory against the French Ministry of Economy and Finance asset-freezing lists, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list for USD and global correspondent banking rails, and reputable PEP databases (World-Check, LexisNexis or equivalent), followed by risk-based enhanced due diligence for any PEP or sanctioned-country nexus, daily or event-driven monitoring, and mandatory suspicious transaction reporting to Tracfin under Article L561-15 of the French Monetary and Financial Code.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI / Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) via the Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; public search portal at data.inpi.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the compulsory language for corporate filings and official documents under the French Constitution, Ordinance No. 58-915 of 7 October 1958, and Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994. The company name must be written in Latin script, may include French accented characters, and any non-Latin source name must be transliterated into Latin characters. A French legal form suffix, usually 'SAS' or 'Société par Actions Simplifiée', must appear on public documents. Foreign words are permitted only where they do not mislead the public or contravene ordre public; all filings submitted through the RNE must be in French, and any foreign-language exhibit must be accompanied by a certified French translation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the Registre National des Entreprises, the applicant will receive a written refusal notification stating the legal ground. The applicant may first submit an informal rectification or a new complete application through the Guichet Unique using a different name. For formal contestation, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the relevant state authority or refer the matter to the president of the competent tribunal judiciaire within the statutory time limit, generally two months from notification. If the name is rejected because of an earlier trademark or trade-name conflict, the applicant may seek cancellation of the prior right in the appropriate commercial court or negotiate a coexistence agreement; alternatively, the affected person may file an opposition with INPI. In parallel, an amended SAS name may be reserved by filing a new registration application.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a non-regulated market-entry consultancy SAS, provided that the address is a genuine French registered office and the domiciliation provider is lawfully authorized under Articles L123-11-2 and R123-220 of the French Commercial Code. The address cannot be a P.O. Box, must be capable of receiving service of process, must be reflected on public registers and tax documents, and must correspond to a real physical location. Virtual-office-only arrangements are not acceptable for regulated financial or payment activities or where bank KYC requires physical attendance; for this low-risk consultancy scope, a licensed virtual office is acceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated annual probability below 10% for a non-regulated service company, absent sanctions or PEP flags. The probability increases materially if UBO screening produces a PEP match, if tax filings are inconsistent with commercial substance, or if the French tax authority launches a tax audit under Articles L12 or L16 of the Livre des procédures fiscales, which may include unannounced physical inspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce): Articles L. 210-1 to L. 210-10 (general incorporation rules), Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-32 (Société par Actions Simplifiée), and Articles R. 123-31 to R. 123-159 (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés filing formalities), supplemented by Decree No. 2023-208 on the single electronic filing window (guichet unique).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Clerk's Office of the Commercial Court) responsible for the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); filings are transmitted electronically through the INPI Guichet unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic single-window creation declaration (dossier unique de création d'entreprise, CERFA M0) submitted via the official portal, together with the final statuts and constitutive annexes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for an SAS (may be set as low as EUR 1). Cash subscriptions must be paid up to at least 50% at incorporation, with the balance callable within five years. Cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked account with a licensed French credit institution, a notary, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the depository's attestation de dépôt des fonds must be produced at filing. In-kind contributions are conclusively released upon transfer of the contributed asset and require a commissaire aux apports valuation report where statutory thresholds are exceeded.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE SHAREHOLDERS. The sole shareholder of FR_SAS, having reviewed the draft Articles of Association, hereby resolves: (1) the Articles are adopted in final form; (2) the share capital has been fully subscribed and allocated as stated therein; (3) the registered office is fixed at the address indicated in the Articles; (4) [Name] is appointed Président, and [Name] is appointed Directeur Général, with the powers conferred by the Articles; (5) the Président is authorized to deposit corporate funds, publish the legal announcement, complete the RCS registration through the INPI guichet unique, and sign all declarations of regularity. This resolution is effective upon signature and remains in force until revoked.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and legal review of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private legal counsel or notary; no government filing at this preliminary stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts in conformity with Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-12 of the French Commercial Code, stating the corporate purpose (advisory services in foreign market entry under ISIC 7020), share capital amount and breakdown, duration (up to 99 years), registered office address, and governance provisions. Secure a physical registered office in France and obtain the landlord's written authorization (attestation de jouissance des locaux) when the premises are leased. Appoint a commissaire aux apports only where in-kind contributions exceed statutory thresholds; otherwise prepare the statement dispensing with such appointment.
required_dossiers: Draft statuts
Registered office lease or ownership proof with lessor authorization
Identity documents of shareholders and proposed directors
Commissaire aux apports report (if in-kind contributions exceed thresholds)
Statement on the non-necessity of a commissaire aux apports (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the draft is later queried by the registry, revise the non-compliant clauses and resubmit without changing the declared activity; no registry fee is incurred at this stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of cash contributions in a blocked account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution (bank), Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or notary escrow
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the company being formed at a French bank or deposit the funds with a notary or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations. Transfer the subscribed cash capital and obtain the attestation de dépôt des fonds (blocking certificate) stating the exact amount and the depository. The funds remain blocked until presentation of the RCS registration certificate (extrait K-bis).
required_dossiers: Bank account opening application
Identity documents of all subscribers
Bank transfer acknowledgements
Attestation de dépôt des fonds issued by the depository
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the account opening, use the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations or a notary escrow; if the blocking certificate contains defects, obtain a corrected attestation before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and signature of the Articles of Association with adoption of the First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders/shareholders acting privately; signature precedes the official filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the constitutive meeting or execute a unanimous written resolution. Adopt the final statuts, subscribe and allocate the share capital, fix the registered office, and appoint the Président and, where desired, the Directeur Général. Verify pagination, signature blocks, and annexes; the pro-forma First Board Resolution records the share subscription, the registered office adoption, and the officer appointments.
required_dossiers: Final signed statuts (original or electronic)
Share subscription and liberation statement
Pro-forma First Board Resolution
Deed of appointment of the Président and Directeur Général
Power of attorney if a representative signs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a signature or pagination defect is detected, re-execute the affected page or the entire statuts before submission; no registry sanction applies if corrected prior to filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal formation notice (annonce légale)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal habilité à recevoir les annonces légales (legal announcement newspaper approved by the local préfecture)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the avis de constitution containing the corporate name, legal form (SAS), share capital, registered office, duration, corporate purpose, and the names of the Président and directors. Deliver the notice to an approved publication organ in the department of the registered office and obtain the attestation de parution (publication certificate). The publication must occur before submission to the guichet unique.
required_dossiers: Project of the avis de constitution
Final statuts approved by the shareholders
Identity details of the directors for publication purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the attestation de parution is delayed, select another approved publication organ; if the published notice contains errors, publish a rectificatif (corrective notice) before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing with the INPI Guichet Unique and RCS registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) single window via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, transmitting to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic creation declaration (CERFA M0 / dossier unique) for a société par actions simplifiée. Attach the signed statuts, attestation de parution, attestation de dépôt des fonds, registered office proof, identity documents, non-conviction declarations, and management appointment deeds. Pay the state filing fee electronically. The guichet unique forwards the dossier to the territorial competent greffe, which verifies legality and, upon approval, registers the company in the RCS.
required_dossiers: Completed electronic M0 creation declaration
Final signed statuts
Attestation de parution of the legal announcement
Attestation de dépôt des fonds
Proof of registered office address and lessor authorization
Identity documents and non-conviction declarations of officers
Power of attorney if filed by a representative
Commissaire aux apports report (if applicable)
Proof of payment of filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffier issues a request for completion or a rejection under Articles R. 123-90 and R. 123-91 of the French Commercial Code, cure the precise omissions and resubmit through the guichet unique within 15 days without additional fee; if the statutory window expires, file a complete new dossier with a further fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration formalities and delivery of the K-bis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for the RCS certificate; INSEE, URSSAF, and the tax administration receive automatic notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, obtain the extrait K-bis and verify all registry data (corporate name, share capital, registered office, directors, SIREN and SIRET numbers). Present the K-bis to the depository to release the blocked funds. Confirm the automatic notifications to URSSAF and the tax administration, and complete any remaining formalities such as the opening of the company bank account and the filing of the CEO mandate.
required_dossiers: Extrait K-bis (registration certificate)
RCS registration order number
Copy of the filed statuts stamped by the greffe
Bank release instruction accompanied by the K-bis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis contains erroneous data, file a corrective modification dossier with the greffe through the guichet unique; if the blocked funds release is refused, provide the bank with the official RCS registration order.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — non-regulated management consultancy under ISIC 7020; administrative oversight for business formalities rests with the local Chambre de Commerce et d'Industrie (CCI), which does not issue any operating permit for this activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no operating or manufacturing licence is required under French law for overseas market entry consultancy services; no statutory professional card or capacity certificate applies.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable — no EIA trigger for office-based consultancy; should physical premises ever exceed ICPE thresholds, the Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) would become competent, which is not the case here.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not required — ISIC 7020 is absent from the nomenclature des installations classées pour la protection de l'environnement (rubriques 1000 to 4000); no environmental registration, authorization, or EIA dossier is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — zero industrial discharges or emissions; the office must nevertheless comply with municipal waste sorting obligations for commercial activities under Articles R. 541-21 et seq. of the French Environmental Code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For leased office premises, verify fire-safety conformity with Articles R. 4227-1 to R. 4227-41 of the French Labour Code (detection, evacuation, extinguishers), obtain an electrical conformity certificate for the fit-out, confirm structural load adequacy via the lessor's lease file, and, if clients are received, classify the premises as an ERP (Établissement Recevant du Public) and complete the corresponding safety commission procedures. Workplace clearance includes registration with the CSE and compliance with general health and safety obligations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — national tax administration responsible for corporate income tax, VAT registration, collection and audit; official taxpayer portal: impots.gouv.fr. Business registration and TIN procurement are performed through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI); local VAT operational unit: Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French-established SAS: (1) incorporate via the INPI Guichet Unique; (2) DGFiP automatically allocates the SIREN (9-digit national company TIN), SIRET (14-digit establishment identifier), and the intra-Community VAT number in the format FR + 2-character key + 9-digit SIREN (11 characters total); (3) obtain the attestation de numéro de TVA intracommunautaire from DGFiP. For a foreign non-established entity: (1) file Form Cerfa 15856 (Demande d'identification pour l'assujettissement à la TVA) with the competent SIE before making the first French taxable supply; (2) provide constitutive documents, proof of foreign establishment and a powers-of-attorney dossier; (3) appoint an approved VAT fiscal representative (représentant fiscal agréé) if established outside the EU (CGI Art. 289 A); (4) receive a non-established French VAT number in the format FR + 2 alphabetic characters + 9 digits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SAS is per se a corporation (Code civil Art. 1843-5; CGI Art. 206) — no US-style check-the-box pass-through election exists; entity-level corporate income tax, VAT and territorial taxes are mandatory. Available statutory elections: (1) fiscal integration (régime d'intégration fiscale) under CGI Art. 223 A for a French parent with 95% or greater ownership of French subsidiaries; (2) election for the normal VAT regime (régime réel) where turnover remains below the franchise exemption threshold; (3) option under CGI Art. 209 quinquies to be taxed on worldwide business profits for companies deriving main turnover abroad (narrowly available and subject to DGFiP conditions); (4) mandatory anti-hybrid qualification rules under CGI Arts. 205-205 C implementing EU ATAD and OECD BEPS Action 2 — no elective hybrid-mismatch treatment is available outside those statutory provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée — TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Established French entity: EUR 37,500 annual taxable turnover for services (consulting) with an EUR 41,250 tolerance limit (2025 fiscal thresholds); below the threshold the franchise en base de TVA exempts supplies but blocks input VAT recovery; crossing the threshold makes VAT registration compulsory from the first euro. Non-established foreign supplier: compulsory registration from EUR 0 (no de minimis) for French-taxable B2B supplies unless the French customer is liable under the reverse charge mechanism (CGI Art. 283-2); B2C supply of distance digital services benefits from the EU-wide EUR 10,000 annual distance-sales threshold under CGI Art. 259-0.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing the e-invoicing and e-reporting reform under the Finance Act of 2024 and Decree No. 2024-255 of 17 March 2024, administered by DGFiP. Domestic B2B invoices must be issued in structured electronic formats (UBL, Factur-X, CII) and routed through an approved Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP) or the DGFiP Public Invoicing Portal (PPF); the mandate applies from 1 September 2026 for large and mid-size enterprises and from 1 September 2027 for SMEs and micro-enterprises. Transaction data (e-reporting) must be transmitted to the PPF generally no later than one business day after issuance, requiring API integration between PDPs and the PPF with digital validation of VAT-relevant fields. France does not operate real-time fiscal stamping or continuous transaction control clearance as seen in Italy or Latin America, but applies near-real-time structured electronic transmission without a live taxpayer clearance step.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Consulting and market-entry advisory services (ISIC 7020) follow the place-of-supply rule under CGI Arts. 259-1 and 259-2: if the business customer is established outside France (EU or third country), the supply is outside the scope of French VAT — effectively zero-rated with the right to deduct input VAT — provided the supplier holds the customer's EU VAT registration number (intra-EU), or a certified foreign tax-residence certificate (non-EU), and can evidence that the service was genuinely rendered to that foreign recipient. Supplies to a French fixed establishment of the foreign customer remain French taxable. Exports of goods to third countries are exempt with deduction under CGI Art. 262-I where customs documentation proves exit from the EU within 12 months; intra-EU movements, if any, require the customer's valid EU TIN and compliance with the French Déclaration d'Échanges de Biens reporting regime.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation / DAU filed electronically via the DELTA ECS platform) evidencing lawful exit of goods from the EU
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport contract demonstrating physical dispatch and destination in a third country
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank certificate or avis de mise à disposition) evidencing receipt of the export consideration in the French entity's bank account
EU VAT registration certificate or foreign tax-residence certificate of the non-French customer supporting the place-of-supply analysis under CGI Art. 259-1
Signed market-entry advisory engagement contract and delivery report evidencing actual performance of the consultancy for the foreign recipient
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP and the French customs authority (DGDDI) may jointly verify zero-rating claims in documentary and post-clearance audits. The ordinary reassessment period is the three-year statute of limitations under LPF Art. L. 169, extended to six years in cases of deliberate tax fraud and further extended or left uncapped in cases of concealed offshore activities or undisclosed foreign flows (LPF Arts. L. 169 B, L. 188 and L. 188 A). Where the exporter fails the substantiation burden under CGI Arts. 259-1 and 262-I, French output VAT is clawed back with: a 40% penalty for omitted or under-declared turnover (CGI Art. 1729-A), an 80% penalty for bad faith (CGI Art. 1729-B), a 100% penalty in cases of abuse of right or organised manoeuvres, monthly late interest of 0.20% per month on VAT reassessed, and criminal sanctions up to EUR 750,000 corporate fine and 5 years' imprisonment for tax fraud or false customs declarations (CGI Arts. 1741-1745; Code des douanes Art. 414).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) in coordination with the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) and the Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (ACPR).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates under a fully liberalized capital and current account regime as a member of the Eurozone and the EU. There are no exchange controls on current account transactions (e.g., trade, services, remittances) or capital account transactions (e.g., FDI, loans, portfolio investments) for residents and non-residents. Profit remittance and dividend distributions are unrestricted, subject to standard corporate tax withholding (if applicable) and anti-money laundering (AML) reporting. The euro is fully convertible; no prior authorization is required for cross-border transfers, but transactions exceeding €10,000 must be reported to the French customs and tax authorities for statistical and AML purposes. Non-resident entities may hold euro-denominated accounts without restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not impose any mandatory surrender or conversion requirements for export proceeds. Exporters may retain foreign currency in designated accounts or convert freely. However, all cross-border transactions must be reported to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics if they exceed €50,000 per transaction or €500,000 annually per counterparty. No specific timeline for repatriation exists, but proceeds must be declared in the annual financial statements and tax returns.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. French-regulated Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto, Shine, and cross-border EMIs like Wise and Revolut Business are viable for operational accounts, offering multi-currency IBANs and low-cost cross-border transfers. However, they may not provide full treasury services (e.g., letters of credit, trade finance) and may have lower transaction limits. Legal constraints: EMIs must be licensed by the ACPR or passport under the EU PSD2; they are subject to strict AML/KYC but are generally more flexible for remote onboarding. For a consultancy with low-risk profile, an EMI is acceptable for day-to-day operations, but a tier-1 bank is recommended for capital escrow or large trade settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for initial corporate account opening at tier-1 banks. Directors (or authorized signatories) must appear in person at a branch or via a notarized power of attorney. Remote opening is possible for certain banks (e.g., BNP Paribas, Société Générale) using video identification and digital signatures, but this is subject to enhanced due diligence and may require a local registered address. For non-resident directors, a physical visit to France or a French consulate may be necessary to complete KYC. The mandate is not absolute; banks may waive physical presence for low-risk entities with strong documentation, but it is prudent to plan for at least one in-person meeting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure (e.g., transactions with sanctioned countries or tax havens)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide detailed business rationale, contracts, and invoices; demonstrate economic substance; obtain legal opinion on sanctions compliance; maintain transaction trail and beneficial ownership documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction patterns (e.g., rapid in-and-out flows, large cash deposits)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide board resolutions, underlying consultancy agreements, and proof of service delivery; maintain a clear audit trail; explain the commercial purpose of each transaction; ensure all payments are routed through banking channels with proper purpose codes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership complexity (e.g., multi-tier offshore holding structures)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full corporate structure chart, register of beneficial owners, and proof of ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) identity; include notarized copies of passports and proof of address; obtain a legal opinion on the structure's legitimacy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient business documentation for a newly incorporated SAS
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the company's articles of association (statuts), Kbis extract (official registry), proof of registered office, and a detailed business plan; include client contracts and projected cash flows to demonstrate operational substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols: Inbound equity injections from foreign shareholders must be routed via SWIFT MT103 with a clear purpose code. For France, the appropriate purpose code for FDI is 'S001' (Direct investment) or 'S002' (Real estate investment) under the Banque de France's balance of payments classification. The transfer must be accompanied by a copy of the shareholder resolution and the updated Kbis. Verification: The receiving bank will require the source of funds declaration (e.g., bank statement from the sending bank) and may request the underlying transaction documents. For amounts exceeding €10,000, the bank will report to the French customs and tax authorities. No prior authorization is needed, but the transaction must be declared in the annual financial statements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: For consultancy services, outbound payments (e.g., subcontractor fees, licensing) are typically executed via SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) or SEPA (for EUR-denominated payments within the EU). For larger trade settlements involving goods, a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) may be used, but this is less common for service-based consultancies. The bank will require supporting documentation (invoices, contracts) and may apply FX conversion at the prevailing rate. For non-EUR payments, the bank will use the correspondent banking network; ensure the beneficiary's IBAN and SWIFT/BIC are accurate to avoid delays.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (deliverable) for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and other major pairs
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for exotic currencies where deliverability is restricted (e.g., certain emerging market currencies)
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) for long-term hedging of principal and interest payments
FX Options (plain vanilla) for flexible hedging strategies
Money Market Hedges (e.g., EUR deposits vs. foreign currency liabilities)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of 0.5% of the tax due per month of delay, capped at 25% of the tax, with potential administrative strike-off after three months of non-compliance
Penalties of 0.5% per month of delay, up to 80% of the tax due, possible company dissolution proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual financial statements with the commercial register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 6 months after the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to 1,500 EUR, potential strike-off for non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit if two of the following criteria are met: turnover exceeding 800,000 EUR, total assets exceeding 400,000 EUR, or average number of employees exceeding 50
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (PCG - Plan Comptable Général)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial ownership information must be declared upon incorporation and updated within one month of any change in ownership or control; no annual confirmation required

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 100-500 USD for registered office and agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 500-2,000 USD depending on company size and audit requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate. Eligible small and medium-sized companies may qualify for a 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to the applicable turnover, capital ownership, and paid-up-capital conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The 15% reduced rate is generally available to companies with turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, at least 75% of whose capital is held by individuals or qualifying companies meeting the statutory ownership test, and whose share capital is fully paid up. Qualifying new companies may access statutory tax-holiday or reduced-rate regimes in designated zones, subject to location, activity, and other conditions. Research and development tax credits and other credits may be available when statutory requirements are met; eligibility is fact-specific.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite. Annual use of carried-forward losses is generally capped at EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. The unused balance may generally be carried forward without a time limit. Carryback is generally available for one year, subject to a EUR 1 million cap and other conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (corporate income tax return), with the applicable corporate tax schedules, including Forms 2050 to 2059-G for companies subject to the normal tax regime, filed electronically through EDI-TDFC or the professional tax account on impots.gouv.fr where available. Form 2069-RCI-SD reports specified tax credits and reductions.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return. Corporate income tax is generally paid through quarterly installments, subject to statutory exemptions and thresholds, with a final balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is generally due within three months after the end of the fiscal year. For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the electronic filing deadline is generally the second working day after 1 May of the following year, subject to the annually published filing calendar and any administrative extension. The corporate tax balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, it is generally due by 15 May. Quarterly installments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD — company identification and accounting-period fields
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SAS legal name, SIREN, registered office, activity, tax office, and accounting-period dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder does not replace the French SAS as the taxpayer. Report the French SAS's French registration and registered-office details; disclose foreign shareholder information where the form or schedules require it.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD — tax regime and return-type boxes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the applicable corporate income tax regime, accounting period, and whether the filing is an initial, amended, or cessation return, as applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned SAS generally files as a French resident corporate taxpayer. Do not select a non-resident regime solely because its shareholders are non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD — taxable result and tax calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the taxable profit or loss and calculate corporate income tax, applying the standard rate or a reduced rate only if all statutory conditions are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the French SAS's taxable results under French tax rules. Apply treaty rules to the shareholder's cross-border income separately; a treaty does not exempt the SAS's French corporate profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Forms 2050–2052 — balance sheet and profit-and-loss account
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report assets, liabilities, equity, revenue, expenses, and accounting profit or loss under the applicable accounting presentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the SAS's French books and transactions. Identify related-party balances and transactions consistently with the supporting records and transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting profit or loss to taxable income, including non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt items, depreciation adjustments, and other statutory tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply French tax rules to all adjustments. Separately identify any cross-border related-party adjustments and retain evidence supporting deductibility and arm's-length pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report tax losses available, utilized, and carried forward, applying the statutory annual utilization limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses belong to the French SAS and are not generally transferable to a non-resident shareholder. Track losses by year and support any utilization with tax computations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report applicable tax credits and reductions, including qualifying research and development credits where relevant.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim a credit only where the SAS satisfies the applicable French statutory conditions and maintains supporting documentation; foreign ownership alone neither grants nor disqualifies eligibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report and pay the final corporate income tax balance through the applicable electronic payment process.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SAS remains responsible for payment even if it is wholly foreign-owned. Ensure the French tax account and payment mandate are operational before the due date.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% where the return is not filed within 30 days after a formal notice and potentially 80% in cases of undisclosed activity or fraud, subject to statutory conditions. Late payment generally attracts a 5% surcharge. Late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, subject to applicable rules. Additional penalties may apply for inaccurate returns, omitted information, or failure to meet electronic filing requirements.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The domestic withholding rate on dividends paid by a French company to a non-resident corporate shareholder is generally 25%, subject to exemptions and treaty relief. Dividends paid to non-resident individuals are generally subject to 12.8% withholding, subject to applicable rules and treaty relief. The EU Parent-Subsidiary regime may exempt qualifying distributions to eligible EU parent companies, subject to ownership, holding-period, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, and other statutory conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the recipient should provide the French payer with the applicable treaty-residence certificate issued by the competent foreign tax authority and the relevant French treaty-relief or refund documentation, including Form 5000-SD and, where applicable, the income-specific Form 5001-SD for dividends, interest, or royalties. The payer should verify residence, beneficial ownership, eligibility, and anti-abuse requirements and apply the reduced rate only where authorized; otherwise, it should withhold at the domestic rate and the recipient may seek a refund using the prescribed process. Treaty rates vary by recipient jurisdiction and income category; confirm the applicable treaty and current administrative procedure for each payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Outbound royalties paid to non-residents are generally subject to 25% French withholding, subject to treaty relief and applicable EU directives. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding under domestic law, subject to exceptions, including specified payments to jurisdictions with privileged tax regimes and other statutory anti-abuse provisions. Treaty rates and exemptions depend on the recipient's jurisdiction, beneficial ownership, instrument, and applicable treaty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: French full transfer-pricing documentation is generally required for a French entity whose annual turnover or gross assets are at least EUR 400 million, or that meets specified ownership or control connections with an entity meeting the threshold. A separate annual simplified transfer-pricing filing, Form 2257-SD, generally applies to qualifying entities at the lower EUR 50 million turnover or gross-assets threshold, subject to the statutory related-party and control conditions. Local-file and master-file requirements and filing deadlines should be tested separately against current law.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no general standalone regime called Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to certain offshore regimes. French tax authorities may nevertheless challenge artificial arrangements under domestic anti-abuse rules, the general abuse-of-law doctrine, the principal-purpose test where applicable, transfer-pricing rules, beneficial-ownership requirements, and treaty anti-abuse provisions. A French SAS should be able to evidence real decision-making, personnel or outsourced functions, premises where appropriate, operational capacity, and commercial rationale consistent with its activities and reported profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion or fraudulent return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing revenue, fabricating deductible expenses, maintaining false accounts, or knowingly filing materially inaccurate returns to evade tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessments, late-payment interest, and surcharges may apply; fraud-related surcharges may reach 80% under applicable conditions. Serious tax fraud may constitute a criminal offense punishable by up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine, with higher penalties in aggravated cases, including up to seven years and EUR 3 million, subject to the applicable statutory provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal liability where they personally participate in or knowingly facilitate an offense. Tax authorities may seek director liability for tax debts in cases of fraudulent maneuvers or serious and repeated breaches that make collection impossible. Imprisonment, fines, asset measures, and restrictions may apply where authorized by law; travel bans are not an automatic consequence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing misstatement or undocumented related-party transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing cross-border related-party services, royalties, financing, or other transactions outside the arm's-length range; failing to maintain required documentation; or making inconsistent disclosures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustments may increase taxable profits and trigger tax, interest, and applicable penalties. Failure to provide required transfer-pricing documentation can attract a minimum penalty generally equal to 0.5% of the amount of transactions concerned, subject to a statutory minimum generally of EUR 10,000 per financial year, and may be increased by reference to tax reassessed, subject to statutory limits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed for intentional fraud or where statutory conditions for personal liability are met. Ordinary transfer-pricing adjustments do not automatically pierce the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful dividend distribution or withholding-tax failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits without satisfying French corporate-law distribution requirements, failing to withhold or remit tax, or claiming treaty relief without substantiated recipient eligibility.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company may be liable for unpaid withholding tax, interest, and applicable penalties. Unlawful distributions may be subject to recovery and corporate-law remedies; knowingly false treaty claims may also trigger tax-fraud sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil or criminal liability for knowingly authorizing unlawful distributions or fraudulent withholding-tax conduct. Personal liability is not automatic and depends on the statutory cause of action and evidence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SAS or contractual arrangements without genuine commercial purpose to obtain an improper tax advantage, conceal the true beneficial owner, or misstate the location of functions and risks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may disregard or recharacterize arrangements, deny treaty benefits or deductions, reassess tax, and impose interest and anti-abuse or fraud surcharges where the required conditions are met. Criminal sanctions require the elements of a separate offense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for their own knowing participation in fraud or other offenses. Corporate separateness is not disregarded merely because the SAS is foreign-owned or has limited operations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing beneficial ownership, knowingly processing criminal proceeds, breaching applicable sanctions, or failing to perform legally required customer due diligence where the SAS is subject to relevant obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sanctions depend on the conduct and applicable regime and may include administrative measures, asset freezing, substantial criminal fines, and imprisonment. AML obligations depend on whether the entity or its activities fall within a regulated or otherwise covered category.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for their own participation, consent, or legally actionable failure to act. Asset restraint or travel restrictions require competent authority action under applicable law and are not automatic corporate-tax penalties.
